title: Mouse without borders says keys dont match, when it does
author: Jebarson
summary: Mouse Without Borders rejects a connection as InvalidKey after settings were restored from a machine running PowerToys 0.100.0 to one running 0.101.2362.0. The report does not yet show whether the mismatch persists when both machines use the same build and regenerate the shared key.

status.label: Matching-version connection test needed
status.detail: The two peers use different PowerToys versions and the key came from a restored backup, so a clean same-version pairing is needed before diagnosing key validation.

next_action.label: Request paired diagnostics
next_action.reason: Establish whether the failure is version/restore-specific or a current Mouse Without Borders connection defect.

judgment.rationale: The log confirms InvalidKey, but the peers are on different PowerToys builds and the shared value was copied from restored settings. Updating both peers and regenerating the key can distinguish stale serialized state from a current protocol defect.
evidence: One machine runs PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 and the other runs 0.100.0.0.
The newer machine restored a backup originating from the 0.100.0.0 machine.
The supplied status text records the remote peer as `InvalidKey`.
No fresh PowerToys diagnostic archives from both peers are attached.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a clean pairing attempt with both machines on the same current PowerToys version and a newly generated key; if it still fails, collect fresh diagnostics from both peers immediately after the attempt.

issue_context.summary: A Mouse Without Borders peer reports InvalidKey after cross-version settings restore and manual key copying.
known_information: Settings from the older installation were restored on the newer machine.
The reporter manually copied the displayed key.
The supplied status output identifies the remote peer and records InvalidKey.
inferences: The failure may be caused by restored or version-specific connection state rather than the visible key text alone.
A same-version clean pairing is required before attributing the failure to current key comparison logic.
issue_context.analysis: The existing text proves the rejection but not which peer or state transition produced it. A newly generated key on matching versions removes the two strongest confounders; paired diagnostics are useful only if that controlled attempt still fails.
initial_investigation: Searched current PowerToys issues for the same InvalidKey wording and found no established duplicate.
The report already includes useful peer topology and status output, so those details should not be requested again.

information_gaps.information: Result of a clean pairing with both machines on the same current PowerToys version and a newly generated security key.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether the failure depends on version skew or restored connection state.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Update both machines, remove the restored pairing, generate a new key on one machine, and enter that new key on the other.

information_gaps.information: Fresh PowerToys diagnostics from both machines if the controlled pairing still reports InvalidKey.
information_gaps.why_needed: Logs from both sides can identify which peer rejects the handshake and why.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Immediately after the failed pairing attempt, submit `/bugreport` from each machine and attach both generated ZIP files, identifying which ZIP came from each peer.

comment.body: Thanks for the peer and status details; the `InvalidKey` line confirms the rejection. Because the machines are on different PowerToys versions and the newer one restored settings from the older installation, please first update both machines to the same current version, remove the restored pairing, generate a new security key, and pair them again. If it still reports `InvalidKey`, immediately submit `/bugreport` from each machine and attach both generated ZIP files, identifying which ZIP belongs to each peer.
